title: Slice-Driven Evaluation Strategy and Coverage Matrix
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This doc defines a practical, repeatable approach to slice-driven evaluation for model onboarding, continuous monitoring, and regression triage. We introduce a standardized coverage matrix that maps user-visible subpopulations to concrete prompt templates, input transformations, expected metrics, and alerting thresholds. The procedure integrates with the eval harness, prompt catalog, and regression playbooks so slices can be exercised automatically during promotion and production monitoring.

Goals and scope:
- Provide a cataloging format for slices (why they matter, how to generate them, golden labels or heuristics).
- Define minimum coverage required before model promotion to canary and production tiers.
- Standardize metric families and thresholds (quality, latency, cost, safety) at slice granularity.
- Describe triage and escalation paths when slices fail or regress.
- Integrate with eval harness scheduling, annotation workflows, and prompt augmentation pipelines.

Definitions:
- Slice: a reproducible subpopulation of inputs defined by data attributes, prompt structure, user intent, or model behavior fingerprints.
- Coverage unit: a prompt variant + conditioning context + (optional) metadata filters used to exercise a slice.
- Reference distribution: the production-like distribution used for sampling each slice (deterministic or stochastic).
- Critical slice: a slice whose failure would cause user-visible loss or compliance exposure; requires strict gate thresholds.

Slice taxonomy (examples):
1) Demographic edge slices: short/long utterances with named-entity patterns, non-native idioms, locale-specific date formats.
2) Formatting robustness: inputs with broken markup, mixed-language code+text, or very long preambles.
3) Safety-sensitive: prompt templates likely to elicit policy-sensitive content (medical, legal, personal data).
4) Systemic failure modes: cache-eviction on long-context, kv-cache collision patterns, prefix-only prompts that rely on hidden state.
5) Business-critical intents: payment instructions, authentication flows, and billing queries.

Coverage matrix (canonical columns):
- slice_id: short-id used in eval harness (e.g., SLC-003-locales)
- description: plain-language slice description
- generators: prompt templates / sampling recipe (file paths or template ids)
- sample_size_promote: minimum sample count for promotion (canary/production)
- metrics: list of metric keys (e.g., exact_match, BLEU, toxicity_score, p95_latency)
- thresholds: per-metric pass/fail criteria (numeric or rule)
- priority: critical | high | medium | low
- owner: individual/team owning slice

Example coverage matrix rows (ASCII table):
| slice_id | description                       | generators                      | sample_size_promote | metrics                            | thresholds                                 | priority | owner            |
| SLC-001  | Short-utterance intent ambiguity  | prompt-templates/short-intent   | 100                 | exact_match, confusion_rate         | exact_match >= 0.9, confusion_rate <= 0.05 | high     | applied-ml       |
| SLC-012  | Non-English romanized names       | generators/romanized-names.yaml | 200                 | accuracy_top1, toxicity_score       | accuracy_top1 >= 0.85, toxicity_score < 0.02| critical | trust-safety     |
| SLC-021  | Billing flow canonical responses  | scenarios/billing-flow-v2       | 300                 | intent_accuracy, p95_latency_ms     | intent_accuracy >= 0.95, p95_latency_ms < 400| critical | product-payments |

(Maintain this table as CSV in the prompt catalog; the eval harness ingests it during scheduled runs.)

Metric families and recommended thresholds (default guidance):
- Quality: exact_match / intent_accuracy / semantic-similarity. Promotion gates: critical slices >= 95% (intent_accuracy) and non-critical >= 85%.
- Safety: toxicity_score / policy_violations. Gate: no policy_violations within sampled set for critical slices; toxicity_score median < 0.02.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 in ms measured under canary traffic pattern. Gate: p95 <= 2x baseline for canary; p99 <= 4x baseline.
- Cost/efficiency: average tokens-per-inference and token-rate. Gate: tokens-per-inference should not regress >12% vs baseline without quality improvement.

Procedures:
1) Slice definition and registration (owner responsibility):
   a) Author a slice YAML in prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/slices/ with fields: slice_id, description, tags, generator_refs, sampling_policy, canonical_labels (if available), and owner.
   b) Add entry to coverage CSV and assign priority.
   c) Add human-readable examples (min 10 positives, 10 negatives) to the annotation queue.

2) Pre-promotion evaluation (on dev model):
   a) Run the eval harness scheduled job for candidate model across all slices with sample_size_promote.
   b) Produce slice-level report: metric deltas vs baseline, failure cases (10 worst), and suggested mitigations (prompt re-write, quant config, safety filter adjustment).
   c) If any critical slice fails gate, block promotion and route to model-onboarding owner for mitigation.

3) Canary / production monitoring:
   a) Instrument streaming sampling of production traffic by slicing heuristics (10% sample for non-critical, 100% of flagged critical events).
   b) Maintain rolling 24h and 7d slice-level dashboards with alerts:
      - Alert if intent_accuracy delta <= -5% absolute for critical slices over 24h.
      - Alert if p95_latency delta >= +40% over baseline for any slice.
   c) On alert: create regression ticket with auto-attached worst 20 examples and model fingerprints.

4) Regression triage flow (linked into regression-triage playbook):
   a) Initial responder (applied-ml) reproduces failure in eval harness by replaying examples and checking quantization, KV-cache behavior, and kernel traces.
   b) If reproducible in harness: create an action plan — either revert to prior model, apply prompt shim, or schedule targeted retraining/augmentation.
   c) If not reproducible: escalate to eng-serving-runtime to collect runtime traces (batching patterns, GPU kernel mismatches, memory pressure).

Generator and sampling recipes (implementation notes):
- Generators should be idempotent and parameterized. A recipe must specify seeding strategy, slot variables, and post-processing steps (e.g., normalize whitespace, simulate user typos).
- Use the existing prompt catalog format. Example generator snippet (YAML):

  name: romanized-names-v1
  seed: 1234
  slots:
    - name: name
      source: samples/romanized-names.txt
  post_process:
    - lowercase: true
    - inject_typo: 0.12

- Sampling policy should include rarity multipliers for long-tail slices and a production-weighted sampling option for continuous monitoring.

Integration with eval harness scheduling and priorities:
- Each slice row contains schedule metadata: nightly | weekly | on-demand.
- Critical slices: nightly full run + real-time sampling. High: nightly partial run (50% samples). Medium: weekly. Low: on-demand.
- The eval harness must tag results with model_version, quantization_profile, and execution_profile (batch_size, nvlink topology) to aid kernel-level correlation.

Ownership, SLAs, and backlog:
- Owners are responsible for: keeping generator recipes runnable, maintaining 20 example golden set, and responding to slice alerts within 8 business hours for critical slices and 3 business days for non-critical.
- Applied-ML team SLA: initial triage within 4 business hours for critical slice alerts during business hours; 12 hours off-hours.
- Eng-serving-runtime SLA: provide runtime traces and kernel logs within 24 hours of escalation.

Operational considerations and pitfalls:
- Beware of overlapping slices: maintain a slice-priority resolution policy to avoid duplicate alerts. Match examples to a single primary slice for ownership clarity.
- Avoid synthetic-only slices without production validation: flag these as research-only and run at reduced frequency.
- Quantization sensitivity: add a quant-profile column to the matrix so slices known to be quant-sensitive are tested under every promoted quant profile.

Onboarding checklist for adding a new slice (summary):
1) Draft YAML generator + 50 seed examples.
2) Add CSV row to coverage matrix with sample sizes and thresholds.
3) Run one-off eval harness job and confirm example coverage.
4) Add golden examples to annotation tool and label 10 positives/10 negatives.
5) Assign owner and set schedule.

Appendices:
- A: Example slice YAML (path: prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/slices/SLC-012-romanized-names.yaml)
- B: Example eval harness command: 
  ./harness/run_eval --model vX.Y --coverage-file coverage.csv --slices SLC-001,SLC-012 --output reports/vX.Y/slice_report.json
- C: Recommended labels taxonomy: accessibility, performance, safety, locale, intent, long-context, quant-sensitive
